title: Effect of GABAergic Treatments on Cortical Plasticity and Motor Learning Capacity in the Subacute Phase After Stroke
official: Effect of GABAergic Treatments on Cortical Plasticity and Motor Learning Capacity in the Subacute Phase After Stroke: a Single-case Experimental Study
summary: The GABAPLAST study explores how commonly prescribed GABAergic drugs prescribed during post-stroke rehabilitation affect cortical plasticity and motor learning capacity. Using a multiple-baseline single-case design, the study evaluates the effects of Baclofen, Oxazepam, and Gabapentin in subacute stroke patients according to their clinical indication. Cortical plasticity capacity is measured with transcranial magnetic stimulation and Paired Associative Stimulation (TMS/PAS). The study aims to determine whether these drugs interfere with or preserve brain plasticity during recovery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults (≥18 years) with ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke in the subacute phase (2 weeks-6 months)
* Non-urgent clinical indication for oxazepam, baclofen or gabapentin, with the protocol-defined treatment initiation interval considered medically acceptable by the investigator
* PGI-S score of at least 2 for the symptom leading to treatment prescription
* Ability to understand and consent (BDAE score \>3)
* Brain MRI available for neuronavigation
* No motor impairment in the non-paretic hand
* Affiliation with a national health insurance system
* Free, informed and written informed consent signed by the participant and the investigator (at the latest on the day of inclusion and before any review required by the research).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Current or recent treatment, within the previous 7 days, with a gabaergic drug of interest (oxazepam, gabapentin, baclofen)
* Current or recent treatment, within the previous 7 days, with any prohibited treatment (benzodiazepine, Z-drug, morphine, pregabalin, sedative antipsychotic or barbiturate).
* History of neurological disorders other than stroke, for example: neurodegenerative disease, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, brain tumour, hydrocephalus.
* History of severe psychiatric conditions, such as schizophrenia or bipolar disorder
* Need for immediate initiation of the planned medication

  * Oxazepam: severe respiratory failure, untreated sleep apnoea syndrome, severe acute or chronic hepatic impairment, myasthenia gravis, hypersensitivity to oxazepam or any excipient, galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption
  * Baclofen: hypersensitivity to baclofen or any excipient, wheat allergy, or coeliac disease
  * Gabapentin: hypersensitivity to gabapentin or any excipient, galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption
* Presence of a psychoactive substance dependence
* Pregnancy or breast-feeding
* Skin disorder in the stimulated hand indicating the placement of electromyographic collection or stimulation electrodes
* Medical contraindications for the performance of MSDs according to the TMS safety questionnaire
* Presence of a major peripheral neuromuscular disorder (e.g. severe motor neuropathy) making the interpretation of PEM unreliable.
* Guardianship, curatorship, safeguarding of justice
